plan_a_advantages: More frequent long runs (4 out of 7 days) which could be beneficial for building overall endurance.
A slightly lower overall volume of training minutes, potentially reducing the risk of overtraining for a runner who isn't currently at a very high mileage level.

reasoning: Plan B is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster, primarily because it incorporates more targeted intensity work and race-specific simulation. While Plan A focuses heavily on longer, easier runs, Plan B includes a dedicated tempo run and hill repeats, directly addressing the need to improve sustainable effort and climbing power – key components of trail speed. Furthermore, Plan B’s longer runs are structured to mimic race distances and elevation gain, providing a more realistic training experience. Plan A’s longer runs are simply longer, without the same level of strategic intensity.
